title: The twin healers
hook: a woman loses a leg in battle; a man is left at sea. the same twin gods arrive both times: the Ashvins
carry: the ashvins: healing is holy work

segments.voice: Yesterday, a king who stalled his vow, and a boy set free. Varuna keeps the vow, and loosens the bond.
screen: `VARUNA KEEPS THE VOW, AND LOOSENS THE BOND.`

segments.voice: A woman goes into battle at night and loses a leg, cut off, the hymn says, like the wing of a bird. A young man is left behind in the sea, three days and nights, with nothing to hold on to. In both stories the same two arrive, fast, in a chariot: twin gods, always called together, never one without the other. They give the woman a leg of iron to walk on. They carry the man home. Today: the gods who come as a pair, the Ashvins.
screen: `A LEG LOST IN BATTLE.` → `A MAN LEFT AT SEA.` → `THE SAME TWO ARRIVE.`

segments.voice: The Ashvins are the twin horsemen of the Rig Veda. Sanskrit even names them in a form kept just for two: Ashvinau, the pair. They're called at daybreak, alongside Ushas, and a long hymn, book one, hymn one hundred sixteen, is a list of their rescues. Bhujyu, left in the sea, carried home in ships that moved by themselves. Vishpala, whose leg was cut off in a night battle: the twins gave her a leg of iron, so she could walk when the fighting was done. A blind man given back his sight. The old sage Chyavana, made young again. Over and over, someone is in trouble, and the twins come. Later tradition calls them the physicians of the gods. The Charaka Samhita, a great classic of Ayurveda, traces its own knowledge down a line that runs from Brahma, through the Ashvins, to Indra, and from Indra to human sages. Here's the teaching. In Hindu tradition, healing isn't outside religion. The gods have their own doctors, and medicine is pictured as knowledge handed down from them. So a family can do puja in the morning and see the surgeon in the afternoon, and neither cancels the other. You could say that for the Vedic poets, a healer arriving in time looked like the gods themselves showing up.
screen: `ASHVINAU: THE PAIR.` · `AN IRON LEG FOR VISHPALA.` · `PHYSICIANS OF THE GODS.` · `PRAYER AND MEDICINE, TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who is sick or healing right now, maybe you. If you pray, hold them in prayer; many Hindus say the old line sarve santu niramayah: may all be free from illness. If you don't, picture the doctors, nurses and helpers around them, and wish their hands steady. Then think of one small thing you could do this week to help someone heal: a call, a meal, a ride.
Hymns to Agni, and today, to the Ashvins: the twin horsemen, called as a pair, who come to rescue and to heal. Today's word.
Your line: the ashvins: healing is holy work. Pray, and see the doctor. See you tomorrow.
